scenes.text: The first New York subway ride was driven by the mayor himself.
On October twenty seventh, nineteen oh four, Mayor George McClellan took the controls at City Hall.
He stayed at the controls all the way up to a hundred and third Street.
The first line was just nine miles long, with twenty eight stations.
That evening, more than one hundred thousand people paid a nickel to ride.
Today, a ride costs three dollars. That's sixty times more.
Would you rather ride the subway in nineteen oh four or today?

title: NYC's first subway train was driven by the mayor 🚇
caption: On Oct 27, 1904, New York's subway opened: 9.1 miles, 28 stations and a 5-cent fare. Mayor George McClellan drove the first train himself, all the way to 103rd Street. 🚇
